raw_response:
I farm 8 mu here in Quzhou. Wheat goes in after the maize comes off in October, then maize after wheat harvest in June. This is how everyone does it here, and this is how I do it. I think about what I did last year and what my neighbors do — that is what works.

For seed, I buy from the dealer in town. For maize I always buy hybrid seed — nobody saves their own maize seed anymore, the ears come out small. For wheat I buy improved seed too, the kind my neighbor Old Wang uses, because he gets good yield.

For fertilizer, I think in bags. One bag is 40 kg. For wheat I put down 1 bag of diammonium (the red bag, for roots) before planting, that is 40 kg per mu. Then when the wheat turns green in spring I spread urea, about half a bag per mu, maybe a bit more — 25 kg. If I put too little the wheat turns yellow and my heart hurts. Better to put a little extra. That gives me around 25 kg of nitrogen, and the phosphorus from the red bag. Potassium I do not add separately — the compound has some, that is enough, the soil here is not bad.

For maize it is the hot season, the plant grows fast. I put 1 bag compound fertilizer (the three-fifteen kind, 40 kg) when I plant, then half a bag urea when the plant is waist-high. Same thinking — do not starve it.

Water: I have a well, thank heavens. Wheat I water 3 times — winter water before freeze, then spring green-up, then at heading. Maize I water 2 times if the rains come, more if dry.

Spray: wheat I spray 2 times — once for weeds, once for aphids and the head disease. Maize I spray 1 time for the borer and weeds together.

Ploughing I rent the tractor, rotary tiller, that is what the service people bring. No one ploughs deep anymore.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize about 550 kg per mu. I expect the same this year.
